paper_metadata.title: Quantum Speedup for Nonreversible Markov Chains

summary: This paper presents two theoretical gate-based quantum algorithms for nonreversible Markov chains: a GQSVT-based reflection through the stationary state with complexity O(sqrt(τ_rev τ) log(1/ε)), and a GQET-based reflection through the most reversible distribution with complexity O(γ(Q_j)^(-1/2) log(1/ε)). The paper reports no hardware experiments, no qubit counts, and no empirical benchmark results; all evidence is asymptotic and illustrative only.

experiments.description: Theoretical quantum algorithm for accelerating sampling from nonreversible Markov chains using generalized quantum singular value transformation (GQSVT) on the curved discriminant, with classical pre-steps to reach a reversibilization time τ_rev.

algorithm.variant: GQSVT on the curved discriminant of a nonreversible Markov chain

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Szegedy quantum walk / projected unitary encoding of the curved discriminant D_{P,P*} using access to P and its time-reversal P*
problem_formulation.objective_function: Construct an approximate reflection 2|π><π|-1 for the stationary distribution π of a nonreversible Markov chain

problem_instance.description: General finite-state ergodic nonreversible Markov chains; no single benchmark instance or dataset is used in experiments.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: The paper is theoretical; performance is analyzed asymptotically and via illustrative figures, not via empirical benchmark runs.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classically run the Markov chain for τ_rev steps before applying the quantum transform.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Amplitude amplification / QMC-style use of the reflection to prepare the target state.

results.unit: uses of Szegedy walk operators R and R*

speedup_claims.factor: up to more-than-quadratic / polynomial speedup in favorable cases; asymptotically O(sqrt(τ_rev τ)) versus O(τ)
speedup_claims.conditions: when the reversibilization time τ_rev is smaller than the mixing time τ
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper is theoretical; no hardware experiment or empirical benchmark is reported.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(τ) for mixing/sampling from the chain

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not reported; no hardware execution, qubit count, or compiled circuit metrics are given.
limiting_factors: No experimental benchmark or device run
Requires access to Szegedy walk operators R and R*
Classical pre-processing time τ_rev may dominate in practice

notes: The paper is theoretical and does not report an actual hardware platform, qubit count, or empirical circuit metrics.
Circuit depth is represented by the asymptotic number of walk-operator uses rather than a compiled depth.
The paper claims a theoretical speedup for sampling from nonreversible Markov chains, with complexity O(sqrt(τ_rev τ) log(1/ε)) in the favorable regime τ_rev << τ.

experiments.description: Theoretical quantum algorithm for accelerating sampling from nonreversible Markov chains using generalized quantum eigenvalue transformation (GQET) on the flat discriminant after a classical number of steps t_rev, targeting the most reversible distribution μ.

algorithm.variant: GQET on the flat discriminant with leading-eigenvalue-selection polynomial

problem_formulation.encoding_details: SPUE of the flat discriminant D_j of P^j, using only the Szegedy walk operator R for P^j
problem_formulation.objective_function: Construct an approximate reflection 2|μ><μ|-1, where μ is the most reversible distribution of the chain

problem_instance.description: General finite-state ergodic nonreversible Markov chains; includes illustrative discussion of a bottlenecked walk on two circles connected by a bridge, but no standalone benchmark dataset is reported.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: The paper provides asymptotic analysis and illustrative numerical figures; no standardized experimental protocol or repeated-run statistics are reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Run the Markov chain classically for t_rev steps until the reversibility-on-π-average condition is met.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Use the resulting reflection in amplitude amplification / QMC routines.

results.unit: uses of the Szegedy walk operator R

speedup_claims.factor: quadratic in the inverse gap of the geometric reversibilization; asymptotically O(γ(Q_j)^(-1/2)) versus classical O(1/γ(Q_j)) when the condition holds
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical mixing/sampling governed by the geometric reversibilization gap
speedup_claims.conditions: when P^j is reversible on π-average, i.e. 1 - <π|D_j|π> << γ(Q_j)
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper provides asymptotic analysis and an illustrative bottlenecked walk; no empirical benchmark or device run is reported.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(τ) for mixing/sampling from the chain

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not reported; no hardware execution, qubit count, or compiled circuit metrics are given.
limiting_factors: No experimental benchmark or device run
Requires access to the flat discriminant and Szegedy walk operator R

notes: The paper is theoretical and does not report actual device execution, qubit counts, or compiled circuit metrics.
The bottlenecked walk in Figure 3 is illustrative, not a hardware experiment.
The paper provides a theoretical construction with complexity O(gamma(Q_j)^(-1/2) log(1/ε)) when the condition 1 - <π|D_j|π> << γ(Q_j) holds.
